summary: This file exports a function that organizes blog posts into series, grouping posts that share the same series name, sorting them by date, and generating metadata objects for each series—including a link, title, image, and a count of published versus draft articles. It's used by Docusaurus to display article collections on a series landing page.

explanations.38: We're creating an empty Map to store series names as keys and arrays of blog posts as values—essentially a lookup table we'll populate as we loop through posts.
explanations.41: We fetch all blog posts including draft ones because we need to count both published and in-progress articles when generating the series summary.
explanations.44: We iterate through each post to check if it belongs to a series; if it does, we add it to the Map under its series name.
explanations.47: We check if this series name already exists in our Map so we don't accidentally overwrite it; if not, we create an empty array for it.
explanations.50: The exclamation mark tells TypeScript we're certain this Map entry exists (we just created it on line 48), so don't worry about null values.
explanations.56: We convert the Map keys (all series names) into an array, sort them alphabetically, then transform each series name into a complete metadata object.
explanations.58: We make a copy of the posts array and sort it by date to find the chronologically first article, which we'll use as the series image.
explanations.62: We count how many posts in this series are published by filtering out drafts; draft posts have a `draft` property set to true.
explanations.72: We use the optional chaining operator to safely grab the image from the earliest post, or fall back to a default image if no posts exist.
